title: Model artifact provenance and signing standard (artifact-manifest-spec)
author: Priya Desai
body:
Summary:

This page defines Redwood's standard for model artifact provenance, on-disk/registry layout, and cryptographic signing/verification for model artifacts deployed to any Redwood runtime (hosted, dedicated, or private). The goal is to ensure reproducibility, tamper detection, and an audit-friendly chain of custody for every model version we serve.

Why this matters:

- Prevent undetected code/model tampering between model training and serving.
- Enable deterministic rollbacks and reproducible inference by capturing metadata at build time.
- Provide a lightweight verification step during deployment and at runtime in Private deployments that require air-gapped verification.

Scope:

Applies to:
- Model binaries (weights) and quantized variants (e.g., .pt, .onnx, .gguf, .pth.q4f),
- Tokenizer artifacts, vocabulary files, and pre/post-processing glue code,
- Model manifests, provenance metadata, and optional build artifacts (container images, layer digests).

Not in scope: training data licensing and raw dataset storage policy (see security-and-compliance/data-management).

Definitions:

- Artifact: Any file necessary to load and run a model (weights, tokenizer, config).
- Manifest: A small JSON document describing artifact components, checksums, build environment, and signature metadata.
- Provenance: Metadata about how and when an artifact was produced (builder, git sha, docker image, quantization profile).
- Signing Key: KMS-backed key (see Keying and trust stores) used to produce an artifact signature.

Principles and requirements:

1) Single-source, machine-readable manifest per model version
- Every model version must include a manifest named manifest.json located adjacent to artifacts (S3 prefix or OCI image label).
- Manifest must be machine-parseable UTF-8 JSON, <= 64KB.

2) Strong checksums and canonicalization
- Artifact blob checksums must be SHA-256 hex digests.
- Manifest must list checksum for every artifact file and the checksum algorithm used.

3) Cryptographic signing and trust chain
- Manifest must be signed using an RSA-PSS or ECDSA key with signature metadata using the COSE compact format (or JWS compact for registries that prefer it).
- Signing keys must be stored in a KMS (hosted: Redwood KMS keys; private: customer-provided KMS/HSM allowed).
- The manifest MUST include the signing key fingerprint (SHA-256 of the public key DER) and the key identifier (e.g., arn:kms:...).

4) Minimal build environment snapshot
- Manifest must include: builder git repo URL and commit, builder image digest (if a container was used), build timestamp (RFC3339), and quantization profile id (if applicable).

5) Immutable storage paths and naming convention
- S3 layout: s3://redwood-models/{org}/{model-name}/versions/{semver-or-timestamp}/artifacts/{filename} and manifest at s3://redwood-models/{org}/{model-name}/versions/{v}/manifest.json
- OCI layout: Put manifest JSON in image label com.redwood.model.manifest (base64-encoded) and attach signature via notation/cosign-compatible mechanism.

6) Verification at deploy time and optional runtime re-checks
- The Redwood deployer must verify manifest signature and all artifact checksums before marking a model version as READY.
- Private/on-prem installations should enable periodic re-verification (default cadence: 24h) and an admin API to force re-verify.

7) Rollout rules and attestation status
- Model versions MUST have an attestation status field in the model catalog: unsigned, signed-unverified, signed-verified. Only signed-verified artifacts are eligible for auto-rollout to production.

Manifest schema (required fields) - line-oriented JSON example:

{
  "schema_version": "redwood-model-manifest.v1",
  "model_name": "{org}/{model}",
  "version": "2026-02-01-rc1",
  "components": [
    { "path": "artifacts/ggml-model.bin", "sha256": "<hex>", "size_bytes": "123456789", "role": "weights" },
    { "path": "artifacts/tokenizer.json", "sha256": "<hex>", "role": "tokenizer" }
  ],
  "build": { "builder_image": "gcr.io/redwood/ml-builder@sha256:...", "git_repo": "git@github.com:redwood/models.git", "git_commit": "abcdef123", "built_at": "2026-02-01T10:12:00Z", "quant_profile": "q4f-latency-1" },
  "signatures": [ { "key_id": "arn:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd", "pubkey_fingerprint": "sha256:...", "alg": "ECDSA_SECP256R1_SHA256", "sig": "<base64>" } ]
}
Notes on the schema:
- components.path is a relative path inside the version prefix.
- size_bytes is required to prevent truncated-download attacks.
- signatures array can contain multiple signatures (builder, QA, security).

Keying and trust stores:

- Hosted: Redwood uses a root signing key stored in Redwood KMS and rotates signing subkeys via an internal signing service. Only the signing service (sig-service.redwood.internal) may generate signatures for public hosted artifacts.
- Dedicated/Private: Customers may configure a key whitelist; manifests signed by an allowed key fingerprint are accepted. When customer KMS is used, the manifest must include the key ARN and an attestor field.
- Blacklist/Revocation: The deployer checks a revocation list (CRL) maintained in the config store. Revoked keys cannot be used for new verifications.

Operational procedures and runbook snippets:

1) How to sign a manifest (CI step)
- Step 1: Build artifacts and write them to staging storage at {s3-prefix}/staging/
- Step 2: Generate manifest.json with all components and build metadata
- Step 3: Use sign-tool (internal) to produce signature:

  $ sign-tool sign --manifest manifest.json --kms-key arn:kms:us-west-2:123:key/abcd --out manifest.signed.json

- sign-tool performs canonical JSON normalization (sorted keys, UTF-8, no whitespace), computes SHA-256 over the canonical bytes, and requests KMS to sign the digest. The resulting signature and key metadata are appended to the manifest.signed.json.
- Step 4: Move artifacts and manifest to final prefix and update model catalog via CLI:

  $ redwood model publish --prefix s3://redwood-models/example/llama-x/versions/2026-02-01-rc1

2) How deployer verifies before rollout
- Deployer steps: fetch manifest, validate JSON schema, verify signatures against allowed keylist, download component checksums (head range if >10MB), verify SHA-256, mark model as signed-verified.

3) Failure modes and alerting
- If signature verification fails: block rollout, create incident with severity P1 if the artifact is in active rollout window.
- If checksum mismatch on a single component: mark version as corrupt, notify owning team, and revert to last-good version if in-flight.
- Telemetry: emit event model.artifact.verify.{success|failure} with fields (model_name, version, verifier_host, failure_reason).

Integration with existing Redwood systems:

- Model Catalog: add fields attestation_status, manifest_ref, verifier_last_checked (RFC3339).
- Console: surface manifest link, signer fingerprint, and build metadata on the version detail page.
- Observability: trace verification as part of deployment span; add SLI for verification latency (target < 5s for manifests < 1MB).

Testing and validation guidelines:

- CI must include a signing/verification smoke test that attempts to verify signed manifests produced in the build pipeline.
- Fuzz tests should simulate truncated artifacts and signature tampering, asserting deployer blocks them.

Migration plan for existing models:

1) Backfill: a batch job will compute manifests for active models and attempt to sign them using the Redwood builder signing key; any models that cannot be reproduced are flagged for manual review.
2) Transition window: new release-automation will refuse to auto-rollout unsigned models after 2026-05-01; teams will receive a deprecation notice by 2026-03-01.

Security considerations and exceptions:

- Exception process: teams may request a temporary exception (valid for up to 30 days) by filing an exception in security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions with justification and mitigation steps.
- Sensitive models: models that include customer PII or regulated outputs must use customer-provided KMS and set confidentiality: restricted in the manifest.

Checklist for model owners (preflight):

1) Build artifacts at a repeatable commit and record git SHA.
2) Produce manifest.json with all required fields.
3) Sign manifest via sign-tool or cosign equivalent.
4) Upload artifacts and manifest to final prefix.
5) Run redwood model publish and confirm attestation_status == signed-verified.

Appendix A — Example verification CLI (usage)

  $ redwood model verify --manifest s3://.../manifest.json
  Verification summary:
    model: example/llama-x
    version: 2026-02-01-rc1
    signatures: 1 verified (key: sha256:... )
    components: 2/2 OK
    status: signed-verified

Appendix B — Helpful snippets and links

- sign-tool repo: git@github.com:redwood/sig-tooling.git
- verification service and APIs: sig-service.redwood.internal (internal docs link)
- Related policies: security-and-compliance/data-management and architecture-and-standards/infra-standards/resource-qos-and-profiling-playbook-2024
